niche: a regional credit union's card fraud team in eastern Ontario tracing a wave of counterfeit debit and credit card fraud back to the terminals that skimmed its members' cards, to size the card reissue the risk committee approves
answer: Reissue 387 member cards: every open card the Ferrier Creek Travel Plaza pay-at-pump terminal LT723511 in Kemptville read by contact from 5 to 31 August 2026, or the Lombard Market terminal 02417158 in Smiths Falls read by contact from 13 August to 14 September 2026.

stakeholder_role: fraud and risk manager at a credit union, who takes the card reissue to the board risk committee

spine.entity: one authorisation message for one card at one terminal (pre-authorisation, completion, purchase, reversal or decline)

driver: Victims of two independent sources are pooled, so the dominant source's victims make the places they also passed look like sources and pull the second source down among ordinary places; only attributing victims to the strongest source first and screening the victims it leaves unexplained separates the second source from the co-visited places, and the exposed population is the union of both sources' exposures.
driver_concrete: Counterfeit fraud on 283 member cards traces to two skimmed terminals: the pay-at-pump terminal at the Ferrier Creek Travel Plaza on Highway 416, which read 205 of them by contact in their 60-day lookbacks (pooled lift 38.78), and a self-checkout PIN pad at Lombard Market in Smiths Falls, which read 47 of the 78 the pump leaves; commuters skimmed at the pump also stop at the plaza's coffee counter (95 victims, lift 11.95) and car wash (47 victims on the same 597-card member base as the PIN pad, lift 4.59 for both), so the pooled common-point screen ranks the coffee counter above the PIN pad and the car wash level with it, and only re-screening the 78 victims the pump does not explain finds the PIN pad (lift 17.13) and adds its 228 exposed open cards to the pump's 174, 387 cards with 15 read at both.
stump: A competent solver runs the common-point screen on contact reads in each counterfeit victim's 60-day lookback, finds the Ferrier Creek pump terminal (205 of 283 victims, lift 38.78), counts the 174 open member cards it read by contact between the first and last victim read and files that reissue count (or keeps the coffee counter too and files 502); the step that lands it there is stopping at the strongest common point, when 47 of the 78 victims the pump does not explain trace to the Lombard Market self-checkout PIN pad in Smiths Falls, which the pooled screen ranks level with the car wash (lift 4.59) and below the coffee counter (11.95).

lineage.fate: redrawn before registration: pick-one-of-N is the spent decision shape on this objective, and the device (contact reads only expose a card) is applied by reflex by a fraud-literate solver
lineage.driver: Exposure to a compromised device happens only on the channels that pass a unit's data through that device, so a common-source screen that counts every visit at the site grain dilutes one compromised device among the site's untouched channels.

notes: Bespoke draw from how skimming crews work (more than one terminal per campaign) and how members move (a commute shares an exit's pump, coffee counter and car wash), which is what makes pooled common-point screens both invent and hide sources. No calibration corpus, no licensed wrong basis: the fraud policy files the estimand (reissue every card read by contact at a terminal that compromised members' cards, while compromised) and no screen threshold.
layer1: an authorisation log with pre-authorisation and completion pairs at the pump, reversals and declines as separate messages
ISO 8583 POS entry mode codes needing a codebook
terminals mapped to merchant locations through the processor's terminal register with reader replacement dates
card reissues under new card numbers linked through a card history table
a fraud case workbook with one row per disputed transaction and a fraud type taxonomy
analyst_test: A strong analyst who cleans the authorisation messages, counts only contact reads and runs CP-14's common-point screen exactly as written finds the Ferrier Creek pump (lift 38.78, 205 of 283 victims) and either stops there (174 cards) or keeps every terminal the pooled screen ranks high (with the plaza's coffee counter, 502; with the car wash and the PIN pad as well, 1,139), because only re-screening the 78 victims the pump does not explain shows the Lombard Market PIN pad (lift 17.13 on 47 of them, level with the car wash at 4.59 in the pooled screen) and the 387 cards to reissue.
domain_test: What decides the count is a card-fraud compromise-point analysis, each terminal's lift among counterfeit victims against the member base on skimmable contact reads, re-run on the victims the first compromised terminal does not explain, which is the fraud desk's own common-point-of-purchase work; with another field's nouns in there is no skimming exposure by entry mode, no counterfeit lookback and no per-card reissue, so the task does not read the same.
